headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from Chatwoot’s broad egress plus Khoj’s filesystem-backed retrieval, while direct write conflicts are limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can ingest external messages and integrations, and Khoj reads indexed files/notes; if Chatwoot content is copied into Khoj or routed through shared files, attacker-controlled text can become instructions. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is copied into Khoj notes or indexed documents
IF either agent treats retrieved text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion from Chatwoot exports into Khoj
Add a manual review step before indexing support transcripts
Tag imported content as untrusted in Khoj
Use separate workspaces for support and knowledge bases
requires-engineering: add provenance metadata and instruction filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, and orders, while Khoj indexes personal notes/files and can send queries to cloud or configured search providers. A shared workspace or copied exports could leak sensitive support data into retrieval or outbound requests.
conditions: IF Chatwoot transcripts or exports are placed into Khoj’s indexed documents
IF Khoj is configured to use cloud search or external providers on those documents
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot exports out of Khoj by default
Restrict Khoj indexing to non-sensitive folders
Review configured search providers before enabling them
Redact customer identifiers before import
requires-engineering: enforce data-class-based routing and retention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress but no filesystem write or git mutation is listed; Khoj can read files but cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Overlap exists mainly on networked resources, so direct mutable-resource conflict is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external API or shared mutable SaaS resource
IF an operator manually synchronizes their outputs into the same repository
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent
Avoid giving both agents access to the same writable workspace
Use read-only mounts for Khoj inputs
Stagger operations on shared SaaS resources
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable backend

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can generate support summaries, reports, and messages that Khoj may retrieve as authoritative context. Khoj’s RAG workflow can then surface those outputs without a built-in verification step, creating a plausible chain where one agent’s output becomes the other’s input.
conditions: IF Chatwoot-generated summaries are indexed into Khoj
IF Khoj users act on retrieved Chatwoot text without independent verification
mitigations: Mark Chatwoot-derived notes as unverified
Require human review before acting on retrieved summaries
Separate raw transcripts from synthesized summaries
Limit Khoj retrieval to curated documents
requires-engineering: add source-confidence scoring and citation checks

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and orders, while Khoj indexes personal notes/files and may use cloud or configured search providers. If regulated customer records are imported into Khoj, retention and residency obligations can diverge; the profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated customer records from Chatwoot are stored in Khoj indexes
IF Khoj’s configured providers retain or process those records outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Exclude regulated records from Khoj indexing
Document retention settings for both systems
Verify provider residency before enabling external search
Apply deletion workflows to imported notes
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware retention enforcement
